entries.title: Grimmett Question 2.2: uniform n-step honeycomb SAW scaling limit
entries.statement: OPEN QUESTION AS POSED IN 2022, current resolution not certified here. Let H be the hexagonal lattice and sample uniformly from all n-step self-avoiding walks starting at its origin. Grimmett asks whether these walks, suitably rescaled as n tends to infinity, converge weakly to an SLE(8/3) random curve. The question does not specify the spatial scale, the continuum endpoint or stopping convention, or a curve topology; any precise proof must state and justify these choices.
assumptions: Uniform law on n-step origin-started honeycomb self-avoiding walks

entries.title: Critical boundary-to-boundary honeycomb SAW conjecture
entries.statement: DISTINCT CONJECTURE. In a simply connected planar domain with two marked boundary points, approximate the domain by a mesh-delta honeycomb subdomain and sample a self-avoiding walk between nearby boundary points with probability proportional to x_c to the number of visited vertices, where x_c=1/sqrt(2+sqrt(2)). Conjecture 1.5 and Section 3.3 of Bauerschmidt, Duminil-Copin, Goodman and Slade predict convergence as delta tends to zero to chordal SLE(8/3). This is a variable-length two-endpoint ensemble; the cited conjecture does not itself settle Grimmett's uniform fixed-length origin-started question.

entries.title: Fixed-length and critical chordal SAW are different ensembles
entries.statement: SOURCE-SCOPE GUARD for P0003. Grimmett Question 2.2 samples a uniform n-step walk from one fixed origin with a free endpoint. The critical chordal conjecture samples walks of variable length between two boundary points with fugacity x_c per visited vertex. The two statements have different length and endpoint conditions. The finite path-deletion, martingale and local-observable identities in this packet do not transfer convergence between them; such a transfer requires an additional theorem.
assumptions: Compare Grimmett Question 2.2 with arXiv:1206.2092 Conjecture 1.5 and Section 3.3

relations.rationale: The scope comparison uses Grimmett's fixed-length, origin-started sampling statement.
The scope comparison uses the separate variable-length, two-boundary-point conjecture.
Both propose an SLE(8/3) scaling limit for honeycomb self-avoiding walks, while their ensembles differ in length and endpoint conditions.
This source-specific question is the Grimmett Question 2.2 represented by the existing P0003 card.
